On every card

What your guests can do

And what comes back to you, in the dashboard, while the cards are still going out on WhatsApp.

RSVP
Attending or not, with a pax limit per reply and a closing date. You see the total pax for the caterer.
Ucapan
A wall of wishes on the card. Hide any message before other guests see it.
Lokasi
Google Maps and Waze buttons, plus add to Google Calendar.
Salam kaut
Bank account with one-tap copy and your DuitNow QR.
Aturcara
The programme of the day, from ketibaan tetamu to bersurai.
Pautan peribadi
A link for each guest with their name on the envelope: "Dengan hormatnya kepada Pak Long Hashim".
Muzik
An original saxophone wedding ballad that starts when the card is opened.
Dua bahasa
The whole card in Bahasa Melayu or English, with Bismillah and doa if you want them.
Senarai hadiah
A gift wishlist with shop links. Guests reserve an item so nobody brings the same rice cooker, and you see who chose what.
Pas tetamu
Every attending guest gets an e-pass with a QR code. Scan it at the door from your phone and watch the pax count fill up.
Peringatan WhatsApp
One tap sends each attending guest a reminder with the date, venue, time and their own code.
Siaran langsung
A Watch live button for family abroad, plus Apple, Outlook and Google calendar.
Reka sendiri
Already have artwork from a designer? Upload it as the front of the card and keep every feature.

Soalan

Questions couples ask

Can I change details after paying?

Yes. Open My cards, choose Edit and save. Guests see the change the next time they open the card.

Do guests need to install anything?

No. The card opens in any phone browser, straight from WhatsApp, Telegram or Instagram.

Can we have two cards, for nikah and bertandang?

Yes. Each card has its own date, venue and RSVP list.

Where do the flowers come from?

They are hand-coloured botanical plates by Pierre-Joseph Redouté and his contemporaries, printed in the early 1800s and now in the public domain.

SandingPrototype build. Payments are simulated. Redouté botanical plates, Cuvilliés rococo frames, old maps of Malaya and Malayan postcards (c.1801–1930) are public domain, via the Cleveland Museum of Art and Wikimedia Commons.
